intent: Individually authored tasks connect materials to stated uses, distinguish iron meanings and preserve temporal states, negative instructions and pollution possibility.

workshop.title: 连材料与用途，辨一词多义
workshop.instruction: 先把使用什么和用途连起来，再用图片辨认iron在原句中的意思，核对材料、时间和条件。

items.label: steel：steel cables是什么，用来做什么？
items.prompt: steel cables是什么，用来做什么？
items.material: The bridge uses steel cables for support.
items.reason: steel是钢，作材料名词通常不可数；steel cables是钢缆。The bridge是主语，uses steel cables说明使用什么，for support说明用途。不要把钢换成铜，或把支撑改成装饰，也不能推广到所有桥梁。

wordDecision.prompt: steel cables是什么，用来做什么？

supportLinks.title: 连起“使用什么”和“用途”
supportLinks.hint: 把steel cables与for support放回对应位置，读清这座桥使用什么、用来做什么。
supportLinks.wrong: 使用的是steel cables，用途是support；不要把桥梁本身或两个关系放错位置。

options.text: The bridge uses cables made of steel to provide support.
options.reason: steel说明缆索材料，for support说明用途。

options.text: The bridge uses copper cables only for decoration.
options.reason: 把材料和用途都改了。

options.text: Every bridge must use the same steel cables.
options.reason: 这座桥的信息不能扩大成所有桥。

items.label: iron：iron在made of后表示材料还是熨斗？
items.prompt: iron在made of后表示材料还是熨斗？
items.material: The gate is made of iron.
items.reason: iron在be made of iron中指铁这种材料，通常不可数。an iron也可以表示一个熨斗，但本句不是说门就是熨斗。先看made of后的材料关系，再定iron的词义。图中左侧示意门的材料明确标为铁，右侧是熨斗。

wordDecision.prompt: iron在made of后表示材料还是熨斗？

art.alt: 虚构词义对比：左侧明确设定为铁制门，右侧是熨斗；区分iron的材料义与可数物品义。

options.text: The gate is made from the metal iron.
options.reason: be made of iron说明门的材料是铁。

options.text: The gate is a clothes iron.
options.reason: iron作熨斗讲可数，但不符合这句made of后的材料义。

items.label: concrete：concrete path在什么时间还暖着？
items.prompt: concrete path在什么时间还暖着？

items.reason: concrete在concrete path中说明混凝土材料；它也可表示具体的，但这里不是抽象与具体的对比。stayed warm表示仍然温暖，after sunset是日落之后。原句没有给出温度数值，也没有说永久温暖。

transfer.stem: Which notes match the exhibition visit?
transfer.passage:
A materials exhibition
Our class visited a materials exhibition at school. The first poster showed a bridge using steel cables for support. Beside it stood a gate made of iron. The guide used the gate to explain how a material name could differ from the name of a household object.
At the next table, we read that copper is often used inside electrical cables. A lightweight frame was labelled as being made of aluminium. We wrote down the material words beside our sketches.
Near the exit, two reminder cards said, "Never mix a cleaning chemical with another product" and "Keep anything containing poison clearly labelled." A water-environment note explained that waste oil can pollute a large amount of water. After sunset, we walked back along the concrete path, which was still warm.

options.text: Steel cables support the bridge; the concrete path remained warm after sunset; waste oil can pollute a large amount of water.
Copper cables only decorate the bridge; the path became cold before sunset; waste oil always cleans water.
Steel cables support the bridge; the concrete path remained warm after sunset; the note gives an exact volume already polluted.
Steel cables support the bridge; the concrete path became cold before sunset; waste oil can pollute a large amount of water.
